questions.stem: An atom has an atomic number of 11 and a mass number of 23. How many neutrons does it contain?
questions.explanation: The number of neutrons is calculated by subtracting the atomic number from the mass number: 23 - 11 = 12 neutrons. The atomic number gives the number of protons, and the mass number is the total of protons plus neutrons.

questions.stem: Where is almost all of the mass of an atom concentrated?

options.text: In the space between the nucleus and the electron shells

questions.explanation: Almost all of an atom's mass is concentrated in the nucleus, which contains protons and neutrons (each with a relative mass of 1). Electrons have negligible mass (about 1/1836 of a proton) so contribute very little to the atom's overall mass.
